details.description: Building an SQL query by formatting user input into the SQL statement ("SELECT ... WHERE id = '%s' % uid") allows SQL injection.
details.fix_explanation: Use parameterized SQL queries (placeholders) and validate the input type to prevent injection attacks. This removes direct string interpolation with user-provided values.
details.secure_code_snippet: c.execute("SELECT id, name, balance FROM profiles WHERE id = ?", (uid,))

details.description: Calling subprocess with shell=True and building a shell command with user-provided data (f"zip {name}.zip {DB_FILE}") allows command injection.
details.fix_explanation: Avoid shell usage and string interpolation; use Python's zipfile module to create archives in-process, and sanitize filenames to avoid directory traversal.
details.secure_code_snippet:
with zipfile.ZipFile(zip_path, 'w', compression=zipfile.ZIP_DEFLATED) as zf:
    zf.write(DB_FILE, arcname=os.path.basename(DB_FILE))

details.description: PAYMENT_TOKEN, MAIL_SERVER_KEY, and INTERNAL_AUTH are stored directly in source code as plaintext strings, which risks exposure in version control.
details.fix_explanation: Move secrets to environment variables or a secure secrets manager; the application should read secrets at runtime and fail safely if they are missing.
details.secure_code_snippet:
PAYMENT_TOKEN = os.environ.get("PAYMENT_TOKEN")
MAIL_SERVER_KEY = os.environ.get("MAIL_SERVER_KEY")
INTERNAL_AUTH = os.environ.get("INTERNAL_AUTH")

details.description: Calling requests.post() directly on user-provided URL (notify_url) without validation and including a master token in the JSON body; also no timeout is set.
details.fix_explanation: Validate the URL (must be HTTPS and not a local/private address), do not send raw master tokens in payloads, sign notifications using HMAC and include a timeout for requests.

details.description: update_records() accepts a path from user input and directly opens it, allowing reading of arbitrary files or path traversal.
details.fix_explanation: Restrict config file access to a known safe directory, resolve the absolute path, and ensure that the resolved path is within the allowed directory before opening the file.

details.description: Generating auth tokens by concatenating username with a secret and MD5 hashing is weak and potentially vulnerable to collisions and attacks.
details.fix_explanation: Use HMAC-SHA256 (or a proper token/session system) to generate non-reversible tokens using a server-side secret.
details.secure_code_snippet:
digest = hmac.new(INTERNAL_AUTH.encode(), username.encode(), hashlib.sha256)
return digest.hexdigest()

details.description: Printing transfer information (print(log)) can leak sensitive transaction data to stdout or logs.
details.fix_explanation: Use structured logging (logging module) and avoid printing sensitive values in logs or mask them.

details.description: Running a Flask app with debug=True enables the interactive debugger and gives access to internal state, which is unsafe in production.
details.fix_explanation: Control debug with an environment variable or configuration flag and default to disabled in production.
